problem_type: Heavy optional Markdown runtime enters the mandatory project-open static graph
symptom: Cold project open imports and parses Markdown/highlighter despite an empty Agent transcript.
direct_cause: Four consumers statically import NomiMarkdown, bypassing the existing LazyNomiMarkdown; Agent resident shell transitively imports the message consumer; the canvas registry is already a dynamic boundary and is not an eager root for the artifact body.
class_root: Production consumers had no single enforced loading boundary separating rendering-on-use from project-open module admission.
affected_population: Every cold shell/canvas project open and future Markdown consumer
Empty projects, image/video-only canvases, actual streaming/skill/prompt/artifact content
entry_points: Skill detail / prompt preview / artifact body direct consumers
internal_only_reason: React.lazy and the existing wrapper are already installed and in use. No new dependency or parser implementation; module-loading admission is an internal renderer owner invariant.
invariants: NomiMarkdown remains the only renderer; every production consumer uses the existing lazy loading boundary
No mandatory project-open static graph reaches the heavy Markdown owner
All original streaming/profile/compact/label props pass through the typed boundary
Surface suspension, lane migration and receipt recovery ownership/order are unchanged; original budgets and fixtures remain fixed

door_reduction.why_not: Four separate UI consumers, one implementation and kernel tests retain their roles, but all production imports converge on one existing lazy boundary; no rendering is duplicated.

generality_proof: The graph regression walks actual TypeScript static imports/reexports from shell and each real direct consumer, so a future indirect consumer cannot silently reintroduce the same eager runtime; type-only contracts and dynamic imports remain separate.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Admit the one heavy renderer only when actual content mounts and preserve its full props
Enforce production module admission from every real consumer graph using TypeScript AST resolution

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Static graph inspection already excludes the renderer owner; artifact component itself remains a direct same-class consumer.

recurrence.reason: Any future static Markdown consumer can reintroduce optional parser/highlighter admission into cold open.
same_class_scan: Compared shell/Agent message path and canvas/artifact path against production CDP trace
rg all common/NomiMarkdown imports and existing LazyNomiMarkdown

prevention.invariant: Mandatory project-open static graph cannot reach the heavy Markdown renderer.
prevention.failure_mode: Class regression fails and reports the exact import path.
prevention.strategy: Remove all direct production imports; preserve typed props at one loading boundary and scan the shell and all direct consumer graphs.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove direct eager imports in the same correction; keep consumers and one renderer.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Existing React lazy boundary and installed Streamdown are retained, with no dependency upgrade.

migration: No persisted data migration; only module admission and typed prop forwarding.
residual_risks: First content use still pays parsing cost, to be checked by real Agent/content walk
Main lane951-module cold overhead remains separately measured; no unsafe migration shortcut
Native Mac/Windows/GPU and full-product performance acceptance remain unverified
